glosses: to contradict

examples.text: До сей мину́ты он находи́л весьма́ полити́чным не о́чень противоре́чить Гру́шеньке, несмотря́ на все её щелчки́, и́бо ви́дно бы́ло, что она́ име́ла над ним каку́ю-то власть.
examples.translation: Till that moment he had thought it discreet not to contradict Grushenka too flatly in spite of her snubbing, since he had something to get out of her.
examples.english: Till that moment he had thought it discreet not to contradict Grushenka too flatly in spite of her snubbing, since he had something to get out of her.

examples.text: His testimony contradicts hers.

glosses: To oppose (a person) by denying the truth or pertinence of a given statement.

glosses: To say things that conflict with each other.

examples.text: The prime minister contradicted herself during her speech.

glosses: To give an order contrary to (another order or wish), oppose (something).

examples.text:

I ever contradicted your desire,

glosses: To give an order contrary to one given by (another person), oppose or resist (someone).

examples.text:

I will haue Gaueston, and you shall know,
What danger tis to stand against your king.

A greater power than we can contradict
Hath thwarted our intents.

glosses: To speak against; to forbid.

glosses: To say something in contradiction to.

examples.text: Les théories alternatives n’ont pas à être cohérentes et peuvent même se contredire les unes les autres sur certains points. Elles reposent sur des anomalies, prétendument inexplicables, qui laissent planer un doute sur certains aspects de la version officielle.

glosses: Le complément du verbe, au lieu de désigner la personne en question, peut désigner ce qu’elle affirme.

examples.text: Ce moyen ne peut être contredit.
